asks: The system prompt dropdown no longer populates all the agent profiles. It only shows the system prompt.

Implement a turn-tail prompting or post-generation injection that send you a prompt at the end of a turn that asks if you have completed all your tasks-> if you respond yes the turn ends, If you ignore it or say no then you just keep working on your tasks.
You just fixed this, but the Monitor -> Reused, Tok/s, VRAM hit rate are not populating again.
I think that monitor->speed->prefill is not populating either.
modify the ./setup.sh file to always generate run*.sh and hypercore*.json files that default to host=0.0.0.0 api_key=0000 and --turn-tail-check enabled by default
you are hung
the message says: no frame for 30.0s
outcomes: Cause. The dropdown is built at run time from `GET /prompts`, and that endpoint reads `ROOT / "prompt.json"` — but this repo ships the profiles in `prompts/prompt.json`.
Against the server running on 8081: So `renderAgents()` in `serve/web/app.js` has nothing to add, and the only entry left is the one hard-coded in `index.html`: "System prompt only".
(`serve/test_prompts.py` had the same wrong path, which is why `test_the_real_prompt_json_offers_the_shipped_profiles` was failing.) Fix — resolve the file instead of assuming where it is:
`serve/prompts.py`: added `PROMPT_FILE` / `PROMPT_PLACES = ("", "prompts")` and `find_prompt_file(root)`, which returns the first of `./prompt.json`, `./prompts/prompt.json` that exists.
A set kept beside the server still wins over the shipped one, and with neither the root path is returned so `catalog` reports it as missing rather than guessing.
`serve/server.py`: `self.prompts_path = agent_prompts.find_prompt_file(ROOT)` (docstring updated to say where the file is looked for).
`serve/test_prompts.py`: the shipped-file test now uses `find_prompt_file(ROOT)`, and a new test covers the search order (root wins over `prompts/`, and neither → the "is not there" error).
The same wrong path is in `/home/ai-agent/HyperCore-CCP/serve/server.py`, which also has no root `prompt.json`; say the word and I'll apply the fix there too.
In openai_to_messages / kw, `enable_thinking` is a kwarg.
With ByteTokenizer, ids are byte values, so we can decode: `bytes(engine.last_prompt).decode()`.
Also: does the mock engine's `max_context` matter?
The mock script "</think>\n\nI wrote the report" — the parser strips the thinking part; the content events are only the text after `</think>`.
So `text` collected from content events = "I wrote the report and the tests for it." Good — the `</think>` is consumed by the parser as reasoning.
The mock script starts with `</think>` so reasoning is empty and content is the rest.
Then `text.strip()` is empty → the turn ends.

outcomes: `pcie-frac 0.00` and `spec-min-p 0.70` are real, in `~/Strata/strata-q2_0.json`.
The Strata config's `pcie-frac 0.00` + `spec-min-p 0.70` is a genuine improvement within the Strata run, but it does not establish Strata over HyperCore.
State file written and validated: `/home/ai-user0/black_box/.mcp_test_state.json`, loop 45, `jq -e '.loop'` returns 45.

One caveat on the numbers. `hypercore-q2_0.log` is a live log and grew during this session (mtime moved from 14:23 to 14:26), so the HyperCore request count shifts between reads: 28 in one pass, 37 in another, median 163.5 vs 162.2.
It is a traceback from `tools/calibrate.py:401`: It died at the first `start_engine` call (`calibrate.py:258`), before any sweep ran.

`/home/ai-user0/.config/hypercore/settings.json` (1498 B, modified 14:17:52) — the actual calibration table, keyed by `GPU|VRAM|CPU|RAM|model|context|mode`: The 2026-10-11 entry is the one that matters for your setup.
Bottom line: no measured `pcie-frac` or `spec-min-p` exists for the current HyperCore config; the calibration ran and deliberately left the defaults in place.
The state file's next step (rebuild, `./setup.sh --calibrate`, record the measured pcie-frac) is still open, and I updated it to note that the attempt needs the GPU free.

That number is not comparable to the calibration's 142.6 base_rate: the API path runs the `reasoning_content` branch, so the token count and decode window differ from the in-process `Session.rate()` measurement.
Both runs are valid and the `MIN_GAIN` gate behaved exactly as coded.
Why 142.0 vs 134.5 is not a comparison. That number is `report["tok_s"]`, the median of two 512-token requests taken at the end of the chain, under each engine's own chosen settings.
HyperCore ran at its defaults, Strata at `pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70`.

`--pcie-frac 0.00` in the Strata config is a no-op value with a side effect. 0.0 is already Strata's default, so writing it changes nothing about the share, but pinning it disables the `PcieAuto` refinement.

What survives unchanged: the gate behaviour, the per-engine decisions, the stale `HYPERCORE_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` in `hypercore-q2_0.json` (confirmed present, and `grep -c "tail skip is on"` on the current log returns 0, so it is still in effect despite the 15:38 run preferring the default), and the recommendation to raise `SWEEP_ROUNDS` or `MIN_GAIN` in `tools/calibrate.py`.
The stale setting is still live: `/proc/1038023/environ` and `/proc/1038022/environ` both show it, and `grep -c "tail skip is on" hypercore-q2_0.log` returns 0.
